question: Is pdf.js rendering performance on WebKitGTK 2.52.6 good enough to be the rendering foundation of a Tauri PDF reader on Linux? (Chrome 155 as reference, not decision-maker)

machine.os: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS, GNOME 46, Wayland session with XWayland

primaryPdf.realPath: /home/tomas-cuevas/Documents/Mega/Libros/Programación/Learning Patterns - Lydia Hallie and Addy Osmani.pdf
primaryPdf.note: symlinked into public/pdf, never copied; range-served over http://127.0.0.1

method.sequential: engines run one at a time, browser killed after every run
method.pdfDelivery: the page fetches the whole PDF into an ArrayBuffer and passes it to getDocument({data}), so render cost is isolated from network/streaming behaviour; fetchMs is reported separately because it is part of first-page latency
method.renderPaths: headline = pdf.js 'default' path (page.render({canvas})), which is what the stock pdf.js viewer does; explicit-context probe re-renders pages with a harness-owned getContext('2d') context
method.rawEvidence: results.raw.jsonl (append-only, every run including the harness self-test), logs/

featureSupport.userAgent: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/155.0.0.0 Safari/537.36

worker.note: pdf.js v6 keeps the PDFWorker on loadingTask._worker; the dedicated-worker port is the Worker object, a fake worker uses LoopbackPort. pdf.js parses in the worker but rasterizes on the main thread.

firstPage.definition: navigationStart -> page 1 rendered AND two rAFs elapsed (canvas visibly composited). rafMs is reported separately because rAF can be throttled in an unfocused window.

randomAccess.definition: getPage(N) + full render + two rAFs, after the sequential phase (page cache warm)

fields.featureSupport.hasWebAssembly: recorded false, actually true: the page tested `typeof WebAssembly === "function"`, but in browsers typeof WebAssembly is "object"
fields.worker.workerType: recorded unknown, actually dedicated-worker: the page expected PDFWorker.port to be a MessagePort, but pdf.js v6 exposes the Worker object itself
fields.errors[worker]: harness self-assertion (see worker.workerType above), not a pdf.js error

comparison.note: worker.workerTypeDerived is recomputed here from raw fields (Worker constructor calls + port class). errors.harnessAssertions counts the harness's own worker self-assertions separately from real pdf.js errors. See harnessArtifactsCorrected for field-level corrections found during the spike.
